chunks: Remember, whosoever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to God. Those who call on others they associate with God, follow nothing but conjecture, and only guess.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about those who associate partners with God?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Yunus, this verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to the polytheists of Mecca, highlighting the absurdity of their blind imitation of ancestors. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi, emphasize the contrast between 'al-zann' (conjecture) and 'al-yaqin' (certainty), illustrating that idolatry lacks the epistemological foundation of divine revelation.
